name: DaVinci Project Library And Media Pool Setup
use_when: A Resolve project needs a clean starting structure before editing begins.
The agent needs backup, sharing, or archive discipline for a Resolve project.
The editor is confusing file browsing with imported project media.
avoid_when: The task is a one-off technical conversion with no Resolve project state.
The project library and media pool have already been organized and locked.
A client has provided a fixed Resolve project structure that must be preserved.

timeline_pattern.pattern: project_library -> named_project -> media_storage_browse -> import_to_media_pool -> bins -> timeline
timeline_pattern.library_rule: Resolve projects live in project libraries; export a .drp backup when sharing or archiving.
timeline_pattern.media_storage_rule: Media Storage is a browser, not the project source of truth.
timeline_pattern.media_pool_rule: Only clips imported into the Media Pool are project media.
timeline_pattern.folder_rule: Drag source folders into the bin list when preserving folder structure matters.

motion.rule: No direct motion rule; good media organization prevents later relinking or missing-overlay problems.

sound.rule: Import production audio into clear bins before syncing or replacing camera scratch audio.

captions.rule: Keep transcript, caption, or subtitle assets in named bins so generated captions are not mistaken for raw source.

color.rule: Keep camera originals and graded exports distinct so color decisions are traceable.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent project setup as a manifest with source paths, clip IDs, media type, intended bins, and backup/export paths.
implementation.remotion: Create a project manifest with assets grouped into bins and a separate timeline composition list.
implementation.blender: Organize linked media, image sequences, and audio references into named collections or folders before scene assembly.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create a project folder and import all used media into grouped tabs or albums before timeline edits.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use a project file with bins for raw video, production audio, music, SFX, graphics, timelines, exports, and backups.

common_mistakes: Assuming a clip is imported because it is visible in Media Storage.
Skipping .drp backups before handoff or major changes.
Flattening useful folder structure during import.
Mixing exports, raw media, and timeline assets in one unlabelled bin.
qc: Is the project in the correct project library?
Was a .drp backup exported before sharing or archiving?
Are all used assets visible in the Media Pool?
Do bins preserve enough source structure to find footage later?
Are raw sources, generated assets, and exports separated clearly?
